svg.title: Bytes versus quality per content type
svg.desc: For each of seven content types, mean LZ4 bytes per frame relative to today's plain quantization (x) against MS-SSIM (y), at 16, 12, 8, 6 and 4 levels, for plain quantization, Bayer 2×2 and Floyd–Steinberg. Floyd–Steinberg sits to the right (more bytes); Bayer 2×2 runs close to plain quantization. Data: results/phase1/report.md.
svg.text: Dithering buys quality with bytes; it does not beat plain quantization at equal quality
Mean over 5 images per type. x: LZ4 bytes per frame vs. today (plain, 16 levels = 100 %). y: MS-SSIM vs. the 8-bit source. Points: 16 → 4 levels, right to left.
How to read: up is better, left is cheaper.
A strategy beats today only if its curve
No curve does by more than ~1 %.
narrowband Phase 1 · 35 images · LZ4_compress_default over packed Gray4, 4 containers per frame
